body:
## Why

#60 adds the first worker, the stay researcher. A **worker** is a subagent the coordinator starts with its `Agent` tool (technical spec section 6). Several of #60's open questions are about what Agent SDK 0.3.301 does, not design choices. This spike answers them in a small project of its own, outside the app. So #60 starts with a pattern that's known to work, and a short example to follow.

The pattern proposed for #60's first open question, on 2026-10-27:

- **The worker's result goes through a tool.** The worker ends by calling a tool, such as `report_result`, whose input schema holds the problems it found and its questions for the user. Its candidates already go through the candidate tools. A `SubagentStop` hook refuses to let the worker finish until it has called it. A `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` then replaces the worker's last message with a result code builds: the candidate lines from the worker's candidate tool calls, plus its problems and questions. So no free text from the worker reaches the coordinator.
- **The worker reads its brief's facts from code.** The `Agent` tool takes only a free-text prompt, so the worker brief (technical spec 5.3) can't have a schema. Most of it is facts code already has: dates, nights, each stop's purpose, set time, and tier, the day's other stops, and the candidates already offered. A worker tool returns those for the stay and stops in its brief. The coordinator writes only what needs its judgment: which stay and stops, roughly when each stop falls, the interests that apply, and what to avoid.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 5.3 (worker briefs) and 6 (workers).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 3 (which agent gets which tool).
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 6 (the `TranscriptAdapter`, for the SDK's `sessionStore` option) and 7 (a restart in the middle of a turn).
- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.7: what #136 found about workers, including that they run in the background unless the coordinator says not to.
- The SDK's types for 0.3.301, in `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts`: `AgentDefinition`, the `SubagentStop` and `PostToolUse` hook types, and `AgentInput` in `sdk-tools.d.ts`.
- The SDK docs: [Subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) and [Hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), the `SubagentStop` and "PostToolUse decision control" sections. The hooks page says a `SubagentStop` hook that blocks "keeps the subagent running and delivers reason to the subagent as its next instruction", and that `updatedToolOutput` "replaces the tool's result" and "must match the tool's output shape".

## Open questions

None of its own. The checks below answer the SDK side of #60's open questions on the worker brief and result, on resuming after a cut-off worker, on background workers, and on how workers get their place searches. #60 settles them, from what this spike finds.

## Do

Build the spike in `scratch/worker-spike/`. `scratch/` is gitignored, so the code never reaches the repo, and it doesn't need to pass `npm run check`. What the next session needs goes in the research doc.

When a choice comes up, make it, and list it in the PR's decisions comment. When something can't be made to work, write down what was tried and what failed, then go on to the next item.

- **Set up a small TypeScript project** with `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` pinned to exactly 0.3.301, the app's version. Sign in to Claude the same way the app does. Give it a coordinator with a short system prompt, on the app's coordinator model (`claude-opus-5-5`), and one worker, on `claude-haiku-5-5`. Give the worker a few fake in-process tools that keep their state in memory: a read of its brief's facts, an add tool that takes a stop ID and one to three items, and `report_result`. No trip data, Postgres, or Google.
- **The result pattern.** Add the `SubagentStop` hook and the `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent`, as in the pattern above. Show:
  - that a worker that tries to finish without calling `report_result` is sent back, and then calls it.
  - the output shape `updatedToolOutput` needs for `Agent`, and that the coordinator sees only the replaced result.
  - how code ties each worker's tool calls to its own `Agent` call, so it can build that worker's result. Check this with two workers running at once.
- **Workers in the foreground.** With two workers sent in one turn, find the setting that keeps both in the foreground, so the coordinator's turn waits for both, and the SDK starts no second turn on its own. Try the definition's `background: false`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` in the Claude Code process's environment. Say whether the two still run at the same time.
- **Each worker's own tools.** Give the worker its own in-process MCP server through its definition's `mcpServers`. Show which tools the coordinator sees, and that it can't call the worker's. Show that the worker doesn't see the coordinator's own tools, or only the ones its `tools` list names.
- **Only our own workers.** Make the `Agent` tool offer only our worker. The SDK docs name `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` for the built-in agents, and an `Agent(fork)` deny rule for forks. Show what the tool's description lists, and what happens when the coordinator is asked to start `general-purpose`, `Explore`, `Plan`, `claude`, or `fork`.
- **Resume after a cut-off worker.** Give the spike a `sessionStore` that writes each line to a file, so a resume takes the same path as the app's `TranscriptAdapter` (persistence design section 6). Stop the process while a worker is running, after it has called a tool. Then resume the session with a new message. Say whether the resume works, and what the coordinator sees for the unfinished `Agent` call. If it doesn't work, try leaving the unfinished lines out of what the store hands back, and say which lines those are.
- **Write the answers into `research/agent-evaluations.md`,** as a new section under Results, after section 2.7. Give each answer with the output that shows it, and a short code example of the pattern that works, with the hooks and the agent definition. Then say, for each of #60's open questions above, what the spike found, so #60 can settle it.

## Done when

- `research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it, and a code example of the working pattern.

## Ends in

A PR with the research doc change.

## Settled in

The PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
